q: The pitch of the note (how high it is) is determined by its ____.
e: Pitch, how high the note is, is set by frequency. Greater frequency, higher pitch. Amplitude sets loudness, not pitch.

q: The greater the frequency, the ____ is the pitch.
e: Pitch is how high the note sounds, and frequency sets it. Raise frequency and pitch rises. Amplitude changes loudness, not high-or-low character.

q: The loudness of the note depends upon the ____ of the wave that produces it.
e: Loudness depends on amplitude: bigger A, more energy, louder note. Intensity is proportional to A squared, and is the objective W m^-2 measure. Loudness itself is a subjective sensation.

q: The greater the amplitude, the louder the note, because more ____ is used to produce a larger amplitude.
e: greater and amplitude have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of greater would describe a different law.

q: If the amplitude of a sound wave is doubled, the loudness is ____ times greater.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective. Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium.

q: Quality of a sound is the characteristic which distinguishes the two sounds of the same loudness and same pitch but emitted by two different ____.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective. Stiffer media generally carry it faster.

q: The notes produced by the violin richer than others because it has more ____.
e: notes and produced have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of notes would describe a different law.

q: Notes of the same pitch played upon different musical instruments are distinguished from each other by their ____.
e: Pitch is how high the note sounds, and frequency sets it. Raise frequency and pitch rises. Amplitude changes loudness, not high-or-low character. Notes of the same pitch played upon cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: The timbre of a sound depends on its waveform, which varies with the number of overtones or ____.
e: Timbre, or quality, lets you tell instruments apart at the same pitch and loudness. Overtones and waveform carry that colour. A violin sounds richer because it has more overtones.

q: The intensity of the sound at a place is the energy transmitted per second per unit ____ held normally to direction of sound.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself. Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium.

q: According to the Eq. (6.7), the intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the ____ of the amplitude of the wave.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself. According to the Eq 6 7 the cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: Loudness is a sensation and hence, unlike intensity, it depends on the ____.
e: In Doppler formulas, fo is what the observer hears and vo is the observer's speed. Plus vo is toward the source, which raises frequency. Away from the source you flip that observer sign. Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2.

q: To the human ears, the loudness of the sound is ____.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective. Padding cuts reverberation by eating the bounces.

q: For a particular volume of sound, some may find it loud, while others finding it ____.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Stiffer media generally carry it faster. Particular volume of sound some may find cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: Normally the greater the intensity, the greater the ____ of the sound is.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself.
